relevance_note: The letter describes identifiable individuals with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants and HA20, for example "The proband (III.1) was an 8-year-old girl of nonconsanguineous Pakistani-Indian descent".
method_note: Read only the paper Markdown, the schema and the rules; all values were copied by hand from the Markdown. Labels: the paper's own labels are used verbatim (III.1, III.2, II.2, II.4, II.1); the unnamed 4-year-old boy of the second family is described only as "The patient" and is the single unnamed patient, so rule 5 gives him the label "patient"; his father has no label and gets "father of patient" (rule 2). Uncertainties and decisions: (1) II.1 is mentioned only as a tested "family member" in the cytokine methods; he is kept as an in-scope relative with all fields not reported. (2) II.4 (died at 17 years of early-onset SLE) is in scope as an affected relative, but the paper never ties a TNFAIP3 variant to him, so he has no variant row. (3) n_patients_reported = 5 (III.1, III.2, II.2, the boy and his father carry a printed TNFAIP3 variant); the authors state no number, so this is my count from the two variant sentences; cohort_size_as_stated is null because no total is stated. (4) The sentence "The additional case of HA20 studied as disease control was sequenced on the Vasculitis and Inflammation Panel." is assumed to refer to the unnamed 4-year-old boy; it is used only as a clinical_diagnosis_basis span. (5) is_proband = false and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = false have span null, because no sentence states those negatives. (6) The paper reports no contradiction between two statements about one person. (7) No table in this paper uses stacked " / " cells. (8) Table E1 normal/negative results (normal lymphocyte subsets, normal nitroblue tetrazolium test, negative infection PCRs) were not turned into phenotypic_features rows; only explicit absences relevant to the person (autoantibodies negative, complement function normal, CRP normal, no genital ulcers, no evidence of malignancy) were recorded. (9) Table E1 gives a haemoglobin of 10 g/L (reference 120-160 g/L), but the authors never call this anaemia or cytopenia, so "cytopenia (autoimmune)" is not reported. (10) "significant steroid-related side effects were noted (weight gain, Cushingoid appearance, and arterial hypertension)" is recorded as a phenotypic feature because the paper reports it as present in subject III.1, although it is iatrogenic. (11) Ethnicity and consanguinity are recorded only for the people the statements name (the proband and the second-family boy); they are left not reported for the sister III.2 and the mother II.2. (12) Vital status is left not reported for III.2 and II.2 although the discussion says they "currently have a much milder phenotype". (13) Age at onset for III.1 is the age of the earliest stated manifestation (choreoretinitis from 6 months); the age at last evaluation is not reported, although the report is written 24 months after baricitinib was started. (14) The father of the boy in the second family is recorded as having oral ulcers and genital ulcers because the paper says he had "similar clinical features" to his son, who presented with "recurrent oral inflammation and penile ulceration"; this is the least direct statement in the extraction and both spans are quoted. (15) "no evidence of malignancy" and "normal C-reactive protein levels" are treated as normal findings (D-27), so the abnormality they rule out is named and marked excluded.

year.span: Journal: The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology (2019)

study_type.span: We report a case of TNFAIP3-mediated autoinflammation manifesting as progressive neuroinflammation.

span: Whole-exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous c.A1939C (NM_001270508) p.T647P variant in TNFAIP3, which was confirmed by using Sanger sequencing in subject III.1 and also present in the symptomatic sibling (subject III.2) and mildly symptomatic mother (subject II.2; Fig 1, A and K).

The patient presented with recurrent oral inflammation and penile ulceration and was heterozygous for the p.N98Tfs25 TNFAIP3 variant, as was his symptomatic father who had similar clinical features from early childhood.

span: PBMCs derived from heterozygotes for the p.T647P variant of TNFAIP3 showed increased expression of NF-κB phosphorylated p65 transcription factor compared with control cells (P = .0124; Fig 1, L).
TNF-stimulated HDFCs from subject III.1 also showed increased molecular weight of Lys63-ubiquitinated NF-κB essential modulator as a result of insufficient A20 deubiquitinase activity (Fig 1, N).

In HDFCs from subject III.1, there was no significant upregulation in binding of TBK1 to the A20 protein in response to TNF-α in contrast to significantly increased binding of A20/TBK1 observed in control cells (Fig 2, G and H).
